gotchas: figma.variables.setBoundVariableForPaint captures the variable's value in the CURRENT resolution context as the paint's raw colour. Applied to a FRAME that already has an explicit mode this is fine, but a fill override set on an INSTANCE keeps that raw colour for rendering, so a Navy-mode example instance came out pure black even though boundVariables.color was correct. Fix: resolve the variable for the mode you want first (walk VARIABLE_ALIAS to the primitive, read valuesByMode[modeId]) and build the paint from that colour, then bind. Same helper is now used for every Tint/Navy example.

Hiding a child of an INSTANCE removes it from that node's `children` array. Iterating indices forward and setting visible=false throws 'cannot set property visible of undefined' on the next one. Hide from the highest index down, or re-read children after every change.

You cannot appendChild into a frame that lives inside an INSTANCE ('Cannot move node. New parent is an instance or is inside of an instance'). To change a nested pictogram in an example, call instance.swapComponent(newComponent) on the existing nested instance.

Setting fontName on a TEXT node that has a text style clears its textStyleId but KEEPS the style's bound fontSize/lineHeight/fontFamily variables. Heading/Display, Heading/H5, Heading/Figure and Heading/Display XL are already Bold, so never re-set fontName on them. Where the design system has no bold variant of a style (bold Body/Small, bold Body/Body in Lifecycle), keep the style applied and bind fontStyle to weight/bold (VariableID:10:25) — or setRangeBoundVariable(start, end, 'fontStyle', …) for a bold run inside a styled paragraph. The audit was widened to accept 'no textStyleId but fontSize + lineHeight + fontFamily all bound'.

Binding lineHeight to line-height/tight (VariableID:308:26, the unitless 1.3 ratio) sets a 1.3 PIXEL line height and collapses the text node to ~2px tall. It also drops the node's fontSize binding. Recovering needs an explicit re-bind of both fontSize and lineHeight to px variables plus textAutoResize = 'WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT' to re-measure.

layoutPositioning = 'ABSOLUTE' throws unless the parent has layoutMode !== NONE. For rail-and-marker diagrams (Lifecycle) build the container as a plain figma.createFrame() and place children by x/y instead.

Changing an auto-layout frame's layoutMode resets its sizing modes: a 327-wide FIXED row became 164 after switching HORIZONTAL → VERTICAL. Re-apply layoutSizingHorizontal = 'FILL' (and the children's) afterwards.

A doc frame created with y = max(child.y + child.height) + 160 drifts once the frames below it grow: five of the six new frames ended up stacked on the same y. Re-stack the whole page in one pass at the end (x = 0, 160 gaps) rather than trusting the per-script offset.

Figma ELLIPSE arcData is the clean way to draw a donut: { startingAngle, endingAngle, innerRadius }, angles in radians with 0 at 3 o'clock and positive running clockwise, so a 12-o'clock start is -π/2. No vector paths needed (cf. the Live operations vectorPaths gotcha).
